profile.summary: hEvo is a family of DNA language models from MulinLab trained on haplotype sequences from human populations, so that the models see real human genetic variation rather than one reference genome. A model reads a DNA sequence of up to 1,024 nucleotides and returns one vector per nucleotide, plus masked-base predictions that can score a single-nucleotide variant as a log-likelihood ratio of the alternative against the reference allele. The authors use it for variant-effect scoring, regulatory annotation and population-genetic analysis.

summary_quotes.text: uses population-scale haplotype sequence variation to learn DNA representations for variant-effect scoring, regulatory annotation, and population-genetic analysis
It is a bidirectional BERT-style masked language model with one token per nucleotide and a maximum context of 1,024 nucleotides.
Use the final-layer nucleotide representations for downstream analyses, or score a single-nucleotide change from masked-base logits.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: hEvo is a bidirectional BERT-style masked language model with one token per nucleotide, in two training stages. Stage I masked 20% of valid nucleotide positions in short contiguous spans and trained the encoder and prediction head together to recover them, with cross entropy computed only at masked positions. Stage II kept the encoder fixed and updated the whole masked-language-modelling head (its dense transformation, LayerNorm and nucleotide decoder) on contexts taken from an observed alternative-allele chromosome with the focal nucleotide masked, sampled equally across five alternative-allele frequency strata. Neither stage used clinical or functional labels. To score a single-nucleotide variant, the variant position is masked once and the log probability of the alternative allele minus that of the reference allele is taken from the same masked context; a positive value means the model prefers the alternative allele. The paper reports that this allelic refinement raised ClinVar AUPRC from 0.471 to 0.904 for its representative corpus with overlapping windows, without retraining the encoder.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README lists primary models hEvo-base and hEvo-large, and public-data variants hEvo-open-base and hEvo-open-large, which are published on Hugging Face as hEVO-base-o (87.1M parameters, 12 layers, hidden size 768) and hEVO-large-o (319.5M parameters, 16 layers, hidden size 1,280). Only the two -o checkpoints are linked for download, and both are gated. The -o models were pretrained separately on public 1000 Genomes Project and HGDP data. The README says hEVO-base-o matches the hEvo-open-base weights by file hash, and that hEVO-large-o has identical tensors to the hEvo-open-large checkpoint after conversion. The model cards pin a code and weights revision in their examples (fa613904 for base, 09541834 for large) and keep the card itself on main. A result should name the checkpoint and that revision.

sections.body: The public GitHub repository holds benchmark evaluators, numerical result tables and figure renderers, not the model code. The pretraining and cohort-preprocessing code sits in a separate Hugging Face repository that is also gated. That repository holds code and placeholder configurations only, without source data, generated training datasets or checkpoints.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Bidirectional transformer with nucleotide-level masked language modelling, one token per nucleotide. The paper's base configuration has 12 transformer blocks with 768-dimensional hidden states and the large configuration 16 blocks with 1,280-dimensional states, about 87 and 319 million parameters; the public checkpoints hEVO-base-o and hEVO-large-o match those two configurations. The sequence encoder feeds a prediction head of a dense transformation, GELU activation, LayerNorm and an untied vocabulary decoder. An optional frequency-embedding branch is disabled by default.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The full-resource models hEvo-base and hEvo-large: 4.784 billion distinct 1,024 bp haplotype strings rebuilt from whole genome sequencing of 63,809 individuals, selected from 550,237 participants across eight cohorts (UK Biobank, TOPMed, HGDP, 1000 Genomes, UK10K, SG10K, CAAPA and an internal Han Chinese cohort). Phased single-nucleotide variants were substituted into GRCh38 in 1,024 bp windows at 128 bp steps, exact duplicate sequences were merged, and Stage I sampled distinct sequences uniformly. Stage II used biallelic SNVs from the phased high-coverage 1000 Genomes panel. The -o models were pretrained separately on public 1000 Genomes and HGDP data alone in both stages, without initialisation from or distillation of the full-resource models.

steps.title: Load the model and embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import torch
from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

REPO = "MulinLab/hEVO-base-o"
# Freeze the checkpoint and its custom code for reproducible inference.
REVISION = "fa6139047c21d92b58bd8eda49ea2f89a884e33c"
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

load_options = dict(revision=REVISION, token=True, trust_remote_code=True)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(REPO, **load_options)
config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
    REPO,
    use_frequency_embedding=False,
    use_flash_attention=False,
    **load_options,
)
assert config.use_frequency_embedding is False
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(
    REPO,
    config=config,
    attn_implementation="eager",
    dtype=torch.float32,
    **load_options,
).to(device).eval()

def encode_dna(sequence):
    sequence = sequence.strip().upper()
    if not 0 < len(sequence) <= config.max_position_embeddings:
        raise ValueError("Provide a sequence of 1 to 1,024 nucleotides.")
    if set(sequence) - set("ACGTN"):
        raise ValueError("DNA must contain only A, C, G, T or N.")
    encoded = tokenizer(sequence, return_tensors="pt", truncation=False)
    # This custom tokenizer returns 1D tensors for a single sequence.
    encoded = {
        key: value.unsqueeze(0) if value.ndim == 1 else value
        for key, value in encoded.items()
    }
    if "attention_mask" not in encoded:
        encoded["attention_mask"] = torch.ones_like(encoded["input_ids"])
    return {key: value.to(device) for key, value in encoded.items()}

sequence = "ACGTTGCATGTCGCATGATGCATGAGAGCT"
inputs = encode_dna(sequence)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(**inputs, output_hidden_states=True, return_dict=True)
    token_embeddings = outputs.hidden_states[-1]  # [batch, length, hidden_size]

    # Optional: summarize the last-layer nucleotide embeddings by mean pooling.
    keep = inputs["attention_mask"].unsqueeze(-1).to(token_embeddings.dtype)
    sequence_embedding = (token_embeddings * keep).sum(dim=1) / keep.sum(
        dim=1
    ).clamp_min(1)

print("Last-layer token embeddings:", tuple(token_embeddings.shape))
print("Mean-pooled sequence embedding:", tuple(sequence_embedding.shape))
EOF

'released' is the Hugging Face repository creation date. The primary models hEvo-base and hEvo-large have no public download, so the structured table lists only the two -o checkpoints, which have their own records (intake-250-20261119-model-hevo-base-o and intake-250-20261119-model-hevo-large-o). The preprint is now saved: bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.10.19.760276 v1, posted 21 October 2026, which the README had referred to without a DOI. Its bioRxiv banner states CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 and its availability statement ends 'Non commercial.', so store_bytes is false and no licence is recorded on the source. The preprint writes the model name hEVO throughout, including for the full-resource models the README calls hEvo-base and hEvo-large. No IP-address stamp was found in the text layer.
